subject: ventures/docker-cache-order-check
professional: a senior DevOps / build engineer who owns CI image builds and reviews Dockerfiles for layer-cache efficiency; first checks: does the canonical 'copy manifest (usually with a glob such as package*.json), install, then COPY . .' layout pass clean, does a Dockerfile whose install really re-runs on every source edit get flagged, and does a real BuildKit rebuild agree with the verdict

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against real BuildKit (docker 29.10.0 / buildx 0.39.0, dockerd started locally, busybox:1.36 base, 'install' simulated by a RUN; scratchpad docker-cache-order-check/cachetest.sh builds, edits src/app.js, rebuilds and reads the CACHED lines). Ground truth vs tool on 5 layouts: (A) Node.js-guide layout 'COPY package*.json ./; RUN npm ci; COPY . .' -> BuildKit: install step CACHED after a source edit; tool: install-missing-manifest-copy (false positive). (B) 'COPY package.json package-lock.json ./; COPY . .; RUN npm ci' -> BuildKit: install re-runs on every source edit; tool: clean (false negative). (C) 'RUN pip install --upgrade pip; COPY requirements.txt .; RUN pip install -r requirements.txt; COPY . .' -> BuildKit CACHED; tool flags line 2 (false positive). (F) 'COPY requirements/ requirements/; RUN pip install -r requirements/base.txt; COPY . .' -> BuildKit CACHED; tool flags (false positive). (E) 'COPY . .; RUN npm ci' -> BuildKit re-runs; tool flags (correct). 1 of 5 right against BuildKit. A 19-case corpus (scratchpad corpus.mjs) adds: 'RUN npm install -g pnpm' before a correct pnpm layout flagged and the real pnpm install never examined; 'RUN apt-get -qq update' alone not flagged (regex needs 'update' directly after apt-get); 'RUN apt-get update' alone, ADD . /app before manifest, go.mod layout, apt combined: correct. The arithmetic of its own three rules on its own test fixtures is right; on the most common real layouts it is wrong.
evidence.completeness: Walked every README/page feature: CLI default scan, path argument, --format json, --fail-on-risk exit 2, --help, discovery of Dockerfile/Dockerfile.*/*.dockerfile skipping node_modules (ran it on ventures/ig-media-pipeline/deploy: 'Scanned 2 Dockerfile(s)'), the page's check button and worked-example button (same engine module imported by index.html), all three finding kinds produced, per-stage reset, COPY --from ignored, JSON-array COPY. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origins. No stubs or TODOs. Gaps: the 'Load worked example (three real issues)' button yields 2 findings of 2 kinds; Poetry/uv/pipenv installs not recognised (not claimed).
evidence.verification: `node --test engine.test.mjs cli.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs`: 49 pass, 0 fail, 178 ms. Seeded 6 mutants with quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (broad-vs-manifest comparison flipped, isBroadCopy length check, apt dist-upgrade dropped from the regex, per-stage reset removed), 2 survived (COPY --from no longer skipped; pnpm-lock.yaml dropped from the manifest regex). Tests only use hand-written layouts that match the author's model; none uses a glob source, a tool-bootstrap install, a requirements directory or a broad copy between manifest and install, so the three main defects below pass the suite. page.test.mjs:111 is titled 'demonstrates all three finding kinds' but asserts two.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (352 lines), cli.mjs, index.html script, engine/page tests. Good: zero dependencies, one engine shared by CLI and page, escapes output, continuation and comment handling. Defects: per-ecosystem state records only the first matching install RUN per stage (engine.mjs:260), so any bootstrap install consumes the slot; manifest matching is literal-filename regex with no glob or directory handling (engine.mjs:208); yarn installRe matches any 'yarn' command ('yarn build'), engine.mjs:57; apt regexes break on flags before the subcommand (engine.mjs:211); the broad-copy test compares against the manifest COPY line instead of the install RUN line (engine.mjs:270).
evidence.claims: Checked 7. Backed: Docker best-practices quote 'Always combine RUN apt-get update with apt-get install in the same statement' (real docs text); the 'Leverage build cache' mechanism FAQ (matches BuildKit behaviour I observed); nothing uploaded (no fetch in index.html/engine.mjs); CLI no network (only fs imports); disclaimer/no-warranty on all three pages; served llms.txt clean. Not backed: 'Load worked example (three real issues)' (2 findings); engine comment 'Every finding kind ... is a real, actionable cache-busting pattern' while it flags the layout the Node.js docs recommend; llms.txt boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice' does not describe a Dockerfile checker.
evidence.fitness: The job: paste a Dockerfile in review and learn whether dependencies reinstall on every build. Walked a standard Node service (COPY package*.json ./ ...) -> told it has no manifest copy, the opposite of the truth; a standard Python service with 'pip install --upgrade pip' first -> flagged at the pip upgrade line; a Dockerfile that really reinstalls every build because COPY . . sits between the manifest copy and npm ci -> 'No cache-order issues found'. With --fail-on-risk as a CI gate it would block correct Dockerfiles and pass broken ones. A build engineer would stop trusting it in the first hour.
evidence.domain: Compared with Docker's build-cache invalidation rules (docs.docker.com/build/cache/: once a layer changes, every later layer is rebuilt; COPY/ADD key on file contents; RUN keys on the command string) and the Dockerfile best-practices apt rule; hadolint (DL3009 etc.) has no order rule for these. The three patterns chosen are real and correctly explained. Departures: the rule that matters is 'is there a context-wide COPY anywhere before the dependency install RUN', but the code asks 'was the broad COPY before the manifest COPY', missing the B layout; manifest identification ignores glob sources (package*.json, requirements*.txt, Gemfile*) and directory copies, which is how most real Dockerfiles copy manifests; package-manager bootstrap installs are treated as the dependency install; apk/yum/dnf update splits are out of scope (stated implicitly).

mutations.change: drop pnpm-lock\.yaml from the npm manifest regex

defects.what: Glob manifest sources are not recognised: 'COPY package*.json ./' (the Node.js Docker guide layout), 'requirements*.txt', 'Gemfile*' fail the literal-filename regex, so a cache-correct Dockerfile is flagged install-missing-manifest-copy (BuildKit shows the install CACHED). Proposed fix: engine.mjs:208 `return sources.some((s) => ecosystem.manifestRe.test(s) || ecosystem.manifestRe.test(s.replace(/[*?]/g, "")));` plus a test; tried in a scratch copy: layout A becomes clean, 49/49 tests still pass

False negative: a broad COPY between the manifest COPY and the install RUN ('COPY package.json ./; COPY . .; RUN npm ci') is reported clean, though BuildKit re-runs the install on every source edit. The check compares the broad copy to the manifest COPY line instead of the install line. Proposed fix: engine.mjs:270 `firstBroadCopyLine < state.manifestCopyLine` -> `firstBroadCopyLine < lineNumber` (and reword the message); tried in a scratch copy: layout B flagged, 49/49 tests pass

Only the first install-looking RUN per ecosystem per stage is examined, so a bootstrap install ('pip install --upgrade pip', 'npm install -g pnpm', 'pip install poetry') is flagged as an install with no manifest copy and the real dependency install after it is never checked (false positive plus masked false negative)
Directory manifest copies ('COPY requirements/ requirements/' then 'pip install -r requirements/base.txt') are not recognised, flagging a cache-correct layout
Tests use only author-modelled layouts: no glob, bootstrap-install, directory-copy or broad-copy-between case; COPY --from skip and pnpm-lock.yaml mutants survive
apt regexes need the subcommand right after apt-get: 'RUN apt-get -qq update' alone is not flagged. Fix: `/\bapt(?:-get)?\s+(?:-\S+\s+)*update\b/i` and the same for install

Worked-example button says 'three real issues' and page.test.mjs:111 is titled 'all three finding kinds', but the example yields 2 findings of 2 kinds. Fix: label '(two real issues)' or add a 'COPY . .; RUN yarn install'-free install line that triggers install-missing-manifest-copy, and assert the third kind
yarn installRe matches any 'yarn' command (yarn build, yarn test), so 'COPY . .; RUN yarn build' is reported as an install
llms.txt boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice' does not describe this tool

verdict: A small, clean, zero-dependency engine shared by CLI and page that picks three genuinely documented cache-busting patterns and explains them correctly. Run against a real BuildKit rebuild it is right on 1 of 5 common layouts: it flags the Node.js-guide 'COPY package*.json ./; RUN npm ci; COPY . .' layout and two cache-correct Python layouts (pip self-upgrade first; requirements directory), while it passes 'COPY package.json ./; COPY . .; RUN npm ci', whose install BuildKit re-runs on every edit. As a --fail-on-risk CI gate it would block correct Dockerfiles and pass broken ones. Tests (49 pass, 4 of 6 mutants caught) cover only layouts the author modelled. Finished for what the README lists; does not meet the bar on correctness, verification or claims. Two of the three high defects are one-line fixes that keep the suite green.
